# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, 12 weeks, US$60,000
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, and has about 1,100 staff.

The Client's AI use spans three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

**Audit finding.** An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems.

**Regulatory drivers.** The stated drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR.

**Certification intent.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is intended to start next year. The start date is not fixed.

**Objective.** The Sponsor stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**Constraints.** Three constraints shape the build:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

**What this means.** The Client needs a working governance system, not a document set. That system must:

- close the inventory finding;
- bring the deployed chatbot under governance;
- establish the gating conditions for the visual inspection pilot before any production decision;
- create a base the Client can carry into ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

In a consulting delivery, an external team writes the artifacts and hands them over. The Client receives documents its own people did not author and may not be able to operate.

In the Guided AI GRC Build, the Client's build team does the work. We provide:

- the method;
- weekly workshops and coaching;
- review of each artifact before the next stage begins.

At Week 12 the Client holds an AI Management System (AIMS) that its General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and internal auditors have built and can run.

This matters for Tamarack for three reasons:

1. **The audit finding needs an owner.** An inventory finding raised by internal audit is closed when the Client owns and maintains the inventory, not when a consultant produces one.
2. **The pilot needs Client ownership.** The visual inspection pilot will move through decisions after Week 12. The people making those decisions need to own the risk register and procedures that govern them.
3. **Certification readiness needs a running system.** ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work next year will require the Client to demonstrate a functioning system with operating evidence, which a handed-over document set does not provide.

**Frameworks.** The program uses two open frameworks:

- the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

**Principles.** Three principles guide the work: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

**Inventory order.** At Week 2, systems enter the inventory in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot first.** It is the only deployed system and the one already interacting with customers.
2. **Visual inspection second.** It is the system tied to the Sponsor's Q2 2027 objective.
3. **Sales forecasting third.** It enters as a planned entry so that it is governed from intake rather than retrofitted.

Further AI systems in use may surface during inventory work. Whether any exist is Unknown.

**Incumbent frameworks.** The Profile Block names an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. It does not state the registers, processes or records these hold. Integration points are therefore marked Unknown unless the Profile Block states the artifact. Each Unknown is confirmed at Week 1.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The readiness themes below indicate alignment only. They do not represent a certification outcome.

| Week | Focus | Tamarack tailoring | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Incumbent integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Confirm steering membership, program dates against the Q2 2027 objective, the two workflow candidates and the works council consultation route | Context, leadership, roles | Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, then visual inspection, then sales forecasting as a planned entry | Scope of the AIMS | June 2026 internal audit finding (stated); ISMS asset records Unknown |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification of the chatbot and visual inspection; confirm with external counsel | Risk assessment planning | Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot: customer interaction, GDPR and EU data location. Visual inspection: product quality and effects on production staff, subject to works council consultation | AI risk and impact assessment | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Treatment plans for both systems, owned by named Client roles | Risk treatment | Unknown |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption; adoption has legal effect, confirm with external counsel | AI policy, leadership commitment | Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle criteria for moving visual inspection from pilot to production | Operational planning and control | QMS procedures Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier arrangements for each system are Unknown and are documented; EU data location requirements apply | Supplier relationships, documented information | Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Human oversight design for the two workflows confirmed at Week 1; works council consultation precedes anything touching production staff | Operation, human oversight | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring for chatbot responses and inspection performance | Performance evaluation | Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change procedures | Nonconformity and improvement | ISMS incident process Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review with the two internal auditors in the build team | Internal audit, management review | Internal audit function (stated); audit plan Unknown |

**Internal auditor independence.** We recommend the Client confirm at Week 1 how its two internal auditors participate. This preserves their independence for future audits of the AIMS.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS. At Week 12 it consists of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**The two governed workflows.** The chatbot is the deployed system and a candidate for one governed workflow. Which second workflow will be in production use by Week 12 is Unknown. This is a Week 1 decision.

**Visual inspection timing.** The production timing of visual inspection relative to Week 12 depends on the program start date, which is Unknown.

**Readiness, not certification.** This outcome is a readiness position. It is not a certification, audit or regulatory compliance outcome.

The figures below are estimates. They include the two-hour workshop, coaching and asynchronous work. Actual effort is Unknown until the build begins.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, team, delivery risks and the decisions needed to start.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, the artifact register, blockers and any scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** receives the minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six elements, an evidence sample index and a 12-month operating plan.

Steering membership beyond the Sponsor is Unknown. We propose the Sponsor confirms membership before Week 1.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Weekly format.** Each week includes:

- one live virtual workshop;
- one coaching session;
- structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

**Scheduling.** Session times will be set once team locations are confirmed. These locations are Unknown.

**Program materials.** Working artifacts are stored in a location the Client designates. Customer data is not required for program materials. Any storage decision follows the Client's EU data constraint; confirm with external counsel.

**External counsel.** The following items carry legal effect and require confirmation with external counsel:

- EU AI Act classification;
- GDPR matters;
- works council consultation;
- policy adoption.

**Price.** The program price is US$60,000. This sits within the US$80,000 budget the Client stated as approved this fiscal year. Fiscal year dates and the payment schedule are Unknown and are set at contracting.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

We propose a contracting call before that date to confirm four items:

1. Program start date, tested against the Q2 2027 objective.
2. Steering membership.
3. Candidate governed workflows.
4. External counsel touchpoints for Weeks 3, 6 and 9.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
